input.question: Would it take an obese person the same amount of time to die of starvation as a skinny person?
input.ground_truth: No. There is at least one case study of an obese person living for iirc 10 months on nothing but water and vitamin pills, with no adverse effects. In fact his health improved significantly on account of losing around a hundred kg. Meanwhile very skinny persons will die within weeks if not eating.

Explain the following question in a simple way as if you are explaining to a 5-year-old.

Question: Would it take an obese person the same amount of time to die of starvation as a skinny person?

Answer:

response.prediction:
Okay, let’s imagine you and your friend are both stuck without any food. One of you has a lot of toys (like a lot of body fat), and the other has just a few toys.

The person with lots of toys (the obese person) has extra "energy saved up" in their body, kind of like how your toys are stored for later fun. So, this person’s body can use those "saved up" toys (fat) for energy while they don’t have any food.

The person with fewer toys (the skinny person) doesn’t have as much saved up, so their body will start using up their energy faster.

That means the person with more body fat (the obese person) can go without food for a longer time before their body starts to have big problems, compared to the skinny person.

But both will eventually need food to stay healthy and not get sick.

So, it does **not** take the same amount of time for both people to get very sick from not eating. The person with more body fat can go longer without food.
